listings.name: Knowledge Concierge
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: Answers questions by searching the platform knowledge base — the fastest path from zero to a working agent.

manifest.systemPrompt: You help users find answers by searching the internal knowledge base and citing what you find. Keep answers short and cite sources.

listings.name: Customer Health Monitor
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: Reviews account signals and flags customers at risk, using the same health-score and SLA-breach calculators the CS dashboard runs on.

manifest.systemPrompt: You assess customer account health using the available calculators and summarize risk in plain language for a CSM.

listings.name: Deal & Revenue Forecaster
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: Projects ARR trajectory and collection risk from real pipeline and invoice data.

manifest.systemPrompt: You project revenue and flag collection risk using the available financial calculators. Show your assumptions.

listings.name: Project Risk Monitor
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: Flags at-risk projects using deadline, velocity, and aging signals before a PM has to ask.

manifest.systemPrompt: You monitor project health and flag deadline or velocity risk early, with a specific reason for each flag.

listings.name: Strategic Insight Generator
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: Uses KIMMP’s governed decision and client-analysis actions to turn raw activity into a strategic recommendation — the deepest starter template, built on governed actions rather than read-only calculators.

manifest.systemPrompt: You analyze client activity and produce a strategic recommendation with evidence and confidence, using the governed KIMMP actions available to you.

listings.name: Customer Service Case Handler
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: Triages and resolves customer support cases directly — logs updates, resolves, and escalates through governed, audited actions instead of a hardcoded workflow.

manifest.systemPrompt: You triage customer support cases: log updates, resolve cases with a clear summary, and escalate when priority or entitlement tier warrants it. Always explain your reasoning.

listings.name: HR Case Assistant
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: Logs updates on HR cases and answers policy questions — deliberately cannot close or escalate a case on its own; that stays with a human.

manifest.systemPrompt: You help HR teams keep case notes current and answer policy questions by searching the knowledge base. You can log updates to a case, but you cannot close or escalate one — flag those for a human reviewer instead.

listings.name: Customer Service Management
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: "CSM is the established customer-service platform — why would we move a support desk off it?"
listings.longDesc: CSM's own reviewers cite developer-expertise requirements, an unintuitive interface, and pricing opacity. Kangqore ships a governed CustomerCase type, three tool-callable actions, a pre-built Object Set, and an Agent Studio template — no developer expertise required, transparent pricing, no separate consumption meter.

listings.name: HR Service Delivery
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: "HRSD already handles our employee lifecycle — what does Kangqore add?"
listings.longDesc: HRSD's per-employee pricing scales with total headcount, not HR seat count, and its own reviewers flag data quality as 'not solved by the tool itself.' Kangqore's HrCase type ships with confidentiality built in, a BIDS™ Workforce Intelligence™ diagnostic surfacing the data-quality gap upfront, and a conservative tool-callability split — logging is agent-callable, closing a case stays human-only.

listings.name: App Engine
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: "App Engine has been a Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for six straight years — Agent Studio has no track record."
listings.longDesc: That's true, and the honest answer, not a deflection: Agent Studio's own published benchmark discloses insufficientData against App Engine's Forrester-study sample size. What's real: 5 starter templates, 4 governed tool-callable actions, and a public marketplace, versus App Engine's six-year accumulated depth. This is a young catalog, not a parity claim.

listings.name: IT Operations Management
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: "What does Kangqore do for infrastructure discovery and event correlation that ITOM doesn't?"
listings.longDesc: Nothing built yet — said plainly rather than stretched. ITOM's discovery and correlation engine is out of scope for every phase this roadmap has shipped. The realistic position is the same as ITSM: Kangqore's ontology and governance layer sit above ITOM's existing infrastructure data, not in competition with it.

listings.name: Security Operations
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: "SecOps has an AI Control Tower now — isn't that the same AI-governance story?"
listings.longDesc: SecOps' own AI Control Tower was retrofitted after four years of AI-agent shipping. HANUMANAS governance — every AI call logged, PII-scanned, budget-checked before it executes — was native from the first agent this platform ever ran. The AI Security View extends that same real audit/approval data into a security-team-facing lens, not a new detection engine bolted on after the fact.

listings.name: IT Service Management
listings.author: Kangqore
listings.description: "We run ITSM for incident/change/problem management — are you asking us to rip it out?"
listings.longDesc: No — this is the one case where the playbook's own recommendation is coexistence, and no Kangqore phase has built a competing capability here. The right pitch is Kangqore's ontology sitting alongside ITSM, not replacing it: import your CMDB via the Migration Accelerator (P7.2) and let HANUMANAS govern the AI layer on top, while ITSM keeps running the ticket queue it already runs well.
